q: At the clinic, Raza told the applicant, “You ____ submit the notice by Friday; it is compulsory.”
e: “Must” expresses strong obligation.

q: Imran said the missing report ____ be in the cabinet at the museum, but was not certain.
e: “Might” expresses uncertain possibility.

q: The man ____ by the door of the clinic is the manager who approved Omar's summary.
e: The present participle forms a reduced relative clause describing the man.

q: At the museum, Hira enjoys ____ historical novels after completing the notice.
e: “Enjoy” is followed by a gerund, not an infinitive.

q: During Iqra's class at the clinic, the students were made ____ the exercise from the report again.
e: In the passive, “be made” is followed by a to-infinitive.

q: The documents ____ by Talha yesterday for the office are beside the report.
e: A past participle forms a reduced passive relative clause: documents that were submitted.

q: At the office, Iqra, the teacher, made the students ____ the exercise in the notice again.
e: The active pattern “make + object” takes the bare infinitive.

q: While preparing the summary at the office, Ali stopped ____ because the phone rang.
e: “Stop doing” means cease an activity already in progress.

q: In a message about the notice sent from the clinic, Hira wrote, “I look forward to ____ from you.”
e: Here “to” is a preposition, so it is followed by a gerund.

q: After reviewing Zara's notice at the clinic, the organisers decided ____ the meeting.
e: “Decide” is followed by a to-infinitive.

q: On the way from the garden with the letter, Sana stopped ____ a phone call.
e: “Stop to do” means pause one activity in order to perform another.

q: ____ the letter at the office, Ali emailed it to the director.
e: A perfect participle shows that the first action was completed before the main action.

q: According to Omar's report, the meeting at the station begins ____ 9:00 a.m.
e: Use “at” with a precise clock time.

q: Ali has worked at the office on the proposal ____ 2023.
e: “Since” introduces the starting point of a continuing period.

q: The policy discussed by Omar at the museum was introduced ____ 2025 and appears in the project.
e: Use “in” with years.

q: At the museum, the agreement concerning Usman's report was signed ____ the two organisations.
e: “Between” is used for a relationship involving two parties.

q: The examination described in Ali's summary will be held at the library ____ Monday.
e: Use “on” with days and dates.

q: According to Iqra's letter at the clinic, the new method is superior ____ the old one.
e: “Superior” is followed by “to,” not “than.”

q: Ali has worked at the garden on the report ____ three years.
e: “For” introduces a period of duration.

q: At the clinic, Hira, the manager of the notice, moved ____ the four assistants and checked each desk.
e: “Among” expresses movement within or surrounded by a group of more than two people.

q: While working on the letter at the office, Hira insisted ____ checking every figure.
e: The verb “insist” is followed by the preposition “on.”

q: At the office, Ali is responsible ____ preparing the final report.
e: The adjective “responsible” is followed by “for.”

q: According to Sadia's letter at the clinic, the match was cancelled ____ heavy rain.
e: “Because of” is followed by a noun phrase; “because” requires a clause.

q: After completing the report at the library, Raza left early ____ the last bus could be caught on time.
e: “So that” introduces the purpose of leaving early.

q: ____ it was raining outside the clinic, the match described in Zara's notice continued.
e: “Although” introduces a concessive finite clause.

q: In Ali's comparison at the office, the first article is inexpensive, ____ the second is more reliable.
e: “Whereas” contrasts two facts or alternatives.

q: The summary assigned to Ali at the museum was difficult; ____, the team completed it on time.
e: “Nevertheless” is a conjunctive adverb showing contrast despite the preceding fact.

q: Before leaving the garden with the notice, Iqra advised, “Take an umbrella ____ it rains.”
e: “In case” introduces a precaution against a possible event.

q: At the clinic, both Hira, the manager, ____ the assistants attended the briefing about the proposal.
e: The correlative conjunction is “both…and.”

q: Under the rule in Zara's letter, you cannot enter the garden ____ you show your identity card.
e: “Unless” means “if not” and introduces a necessary condition.

q: At the garden, Omar stayed late ____ the report could be completed.
e: “So that” introduces purpose or intended result.
